# awscc_mediaconnect_router_output (Data Source)

Data Source schema for AWS::MediaConnect::RouterOutput



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) Uniquely identifies the resource.

### Read-Only

- `arn` (String)
- `associated_source_endpoint_arns` (List of String) The Amazon Resource Names (ARNs) of one or more source endpoints that are associated with this router output.
- `availability_zone` (String) The Availability Zone where you want to create the router output. This must be a valid Availability Zone for the region specified by regionName, or the current region if no regionName is provided.
- `configuration` (Attributes) The configuration settings for a router output. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration))
- `created_at` (String) The timestamp when the router output was created.
- `fabric_configuration` (Attributes) The fabric configuration settings for the router output. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--fabric_configuration))
- `ip_address` (String) The IP address of the router output.
- `maintenance_configuration` (Attributes) The configuration settings for maintenance operations, including preferred maintenance windows and schedules. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--maintenance_configuration))
- `maintenance_type` (String)
- `maximum_bitrate` (Number) The maximum bitrate for the router output.
- `name` (String) The name of the router output.
- `output_type` (String)
- `region_name` (String) The Amazon Web Services Region for the router output. Defaults to the current region if not specified.
- `routed_state` (String)
- `router_output_id` (String) The unique identifier of the router output.
- `routing_scope` (String)
- `state` (String)
- `tags` (Attributes List) Key-value pairs that can be used to tag this router output. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tags))
- `tier` (String)
- `updated_at` (String) The timestamp when the router output was last updated.

<a id="nestedatt--configuration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration`

Read-Only:

- `media_connect_flow` (Attributes) Configuration settings for connecting a router output to a MediaConnect flow source. To connect the router output to the flow source, provide both flowArn and flowSourceArn. To disconnect it, call the update operation and omit both fields while keeping this configuration object. You can't change destinationTransitEncryption while the router output is connected to a flow source. To change it, first disconnect the router output, then update the encryption. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--media_connect_flow))
- `media_live_input` (Attributes) Configuration settings for connecting a router output to a MediaLive input. To connect the router output to the MediaLive input, provide both mediaLiveInputArn and mediaLivePipelineId. To disconnect it, call the update operation and omit both fields while keeping this configuration object. You can't change destinationTransitEncryption while the router output is connected to a MediaLive input. To change it, first disconnect the router output, then update the encryption. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--media_live_input))
- `source_endpoint` (Attributes) Configuration settings for a router output that is represented by a source endpoint. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--source_endpoint))
- `standard` (Attributes) The configuration settings for a standard router output, including the protocol, protocol-specific configuration, network interface, and availability zone. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard))

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--source_endpoint"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.source_endpoint`

Read-Only:

- `destination_transit_encryption` (Attributes) The encryption settings for an endpoint connection. This is a union type, so exactly one of its members is set: secretsManager when you store the encryption key or passphrase in Secrets Manager, or automatic when you let MediaConnect determine the encryption key when the endpoint connects. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--source_endpoint--destination_transit_encryption))
- `destination_transit_encryption_type` (String)
- `endpoint_lifecycle_management` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--source_endpoint--destination_transit_encryption"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.source_endpoint.destination_transit_encryption`

Read-Only:

- `automatic` (String) The configuration for automatic endpoint encryption. In this mode, MediaConnect determines the encryption key when the endpoint connects. This type does not require any additional settings.
- `secrets_manager` (Attributes) The endpoint encryption configuration for connections that use a key or passphrase that you store in Secrets Manager. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--source_endpoint--destination_transit_encryption--secrets_manager))

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--source_endpoint--destination_transit_encryption--secrets_manager"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.source_endpoint.destination_transit_encryption.secrets_manager`

Read-Only:

- `encryption_secret` (Attributes) The configuration for the Secrets Manager secret that holds the key or passphrase used to encrypt an endpoint connection. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--source_endpoint--destination_transit_encryption--secrets_manager--encryption_secret))
- `encryption_secret_type` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--source_endpoint--destination_transit_encryption--secrets_manager--encryption_secret"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.source_endpoint.destination_transit_encryption.secrets_manager.encryption_secret`

Read-Only:

- `secret_arn` (String) The ARN of the Secrets Manager secret that holds the key or passphrase. The secret must be encrypted with a customer managed Amazon Web Services KMS key that is enabled and symmetric; it cannot use the Amazon Web Services managed key aws/secretsmanager. The secret must be in the same Amazon Web Services account and Region as the endpoint.





<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard`

Read-Only:

- `network_interface_arn` (String) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the network interface associated with the standard router output.
- `protocol` (String)
- `protocol_configuration` (Attributes) The protocol configuration settings for a router output. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration))

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard.protocol_configuration`

Read-Only:

- `rist` (Attributes) The configuration settings for a router output using the RIST (Reliable Internet Stream Transport) protocol, including the destination address and port. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--rist))
- `rtmp_push` (Attributes) The configuration settings for a router output that pushes a stream to a destination using the RTMP (Real-Time Messaging Protocol) protocol, or RTMPS (RTMP over TLS) when TLS encryption is specified. These settings include the destination address and port, the application and stream names, and optional TLS encryption configuration. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--rtmp_push))
- `rtp` (Attributes) The configuration settings for a router output using the RTP (Real-Time Transport Protocol) protocol, including the destination address and port, and forward error correction state. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--rtp))
- `srt_caller` (Attributes) The configuration settings for a router output using the SRT (Secure Reliable Transport) protocol in caller mode, including the destination address and port, minimum latency, stream ID, and encryption key configuration. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--srt_caller))
- `srt_listener` (Attributes) The configuration settings for a router output using the SRT (Secure Reliable Transport) protocol in listener mode, including the port, minimum latency, and encryption key configuration. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--srt_listener))

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--rist"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard.protocol_configuration.rist`

Read-Only:

- `destination_address` (String) The destination IP address for the RIST protocol in the router output configuration.
- `destination_port` (Number) The destination port number for the RIST protocol in the router output configuration.


<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--rtmp_push"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard.protocol_configuration.rtmp_push`

Read-Only:

- `application_name` (String) The name of the RTMP application on the destination server. Together with the stream name, the application name forms the RTMP URL path, in the pattern rtmp://destinationAddress/applicationName/streamName.
- `destination_address` (String) The IP address or hostname of the destination RTMP server that the router output pushes the stream to. Provide only the server address; specify the application and stream names separately.
- `destination_port` (Number) The TCP port on the destination RTMP server. For RTMP, valid values range from 1024 to 65535. For RTMPS (RTMP over TLS), valid values are 443 or 1024 to 65535. RTMP typically uses port 1935, and RTMPS typically uses port 443.
- `stream_name` (String) The name of the RTMP stream that the output publishes to the destination application. The stream name forms the final segment of the RTMP URL path.
- `tls_encryption` (Attributes) The Transport Layer Security (TLS) encryption settings used to establish a secure connection to a destination. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--rtmp_push--tls_encryption))

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--rtmp_push--tls_encryption"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard.protocol_configuration.rtmp_push.tls_encryption`

Read-Only:

- `encryption_configuration` (Attributes) The configuration settings for TLS encryption. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--rtmp_push--tls_encryption--encryption_configuration))
- `encryption_type` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--configuration--standard--protocol_configuration--rtmp_push--tls_encryption--encryption_configuration"></a>
### Nested Schema for `configuration.standard.protocol_configuration.rtmp_push.tls_encryption.encryption_configuration`

Read-Only:

- `public` (String) The TLS encryption configuration for destinations that present a certificate from a publicly trusted certificate authority. This type does not require any additional settings.

- `destination_port` (Number) The destination port number for the RTP protocol in the router output configuration.
- `forward_error_correction` (String)
